title: Stop harassing businessmen : Opposition MP
byline: The Government has to stop harassing local businessmen, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake said focusing on the arrest of House of Fashion owner whom he revealed has been sent behind bars for undervaluing his assets.

title: Dengue threat to continue till mid-August: Health Minister
byline: Excepting for three districts, a decreasing trend of the dengue outbreak could be seen in the country.

title: France becomes first EU country to ban social media access for under-15s
byline: France’s parliament has approved a bill banning social media access for children under 15, making it the first EU country to bar children from apps such as TikTok.

title: Government undecided over bringing new Constitution: Nalinda
byline: Even after nearly two years since the Government came into power, Cabinet spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa said yesterday the Government has still not decided whether to bring in a new Constitution.

title: Way forward for victims of Microfinance crisis towards recovery
byline: Following the recent enactment of the Microfinance and Money Lending Act, the Avanka Lanka Foundation has issued an open letter urging President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to grant special approval for over two million debt-trapped Sri Lankans to form dedicated, village-based Thrift and Credit Cooperative Societies.

title: Cruelty accounts for most child abuse cases in Sri Lanka
byline: Cruelty has remained the most frequently reported form of child abuse to the National Child Protection Authority (NCPA) over the past 15 years, according to official statistics released by the Department of Census and Statistics.

title: US $ 715 million siphoned off on false import documents
byline: In what appeared to be a massive financial irregularity, the police informed the Committee on Public Finance (CoPF) yesterday that approximately US$ 715 million (Rs. 240 billion) , is likely to have been earned through criminal activities such as drug trafficking, had been remitted on false import documents, an official said yesterday.

title: More than 140 dead, missing on refugee boat stranded off Mauritania
byline: At least 143 refugees and migrants are dead or missing from a single boat off the coast of Mauritania that was trying to reach Europe, the United Nations refugee agency, UNHCR, says.

title: Feasibility study begins for landmark Canal-Top Solar Project over Vienna Canal
byline: A preliminary feasibility study has been launched to introduce a Canal-Top Solar Power Project above the Vienna Canal in Mahiyangana, following a concept proposed by Plantations and Community Infrastructure Minister Samantha Vidyarathna.

title: Gunmen open fire at Devinuwara house
byline: A group of unidentified individuals who arrived in a car opened fire at a house behind the Devinuwara Sri Vishnu Devalaya before fleeing the scene, police said.

title: Three-wheeler plunges into Mohini Ella ravine, two killed
byline: Two people were killed and two children were critically injured after a three-wheeler traveling from Nallathanniya towards Maskeliya plunged down a steep ravine near Mohini Ella, police said.

title: Central Bank keeps policy rate at 8.75% due to inflation rise
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has decided to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 8.75%, citing the need to carefully assess evolving domestic and global economic conditions.

title: Godzilla vs Kong actress Kaylee Hottle dies in crash at 18
byline: US actress Kaylee Hottle, who starred in the Godzilla vs Kong movie series, has died in a car crash at age 18.

title: Four-hour water cut in several Kandy areas today
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced that water supply to several areas in Kandy will be temporarily suspended for four hours today (22) due to essential maintenance work at the Kandy Main Water Supply Project.

title: Iran war has cost US $37.5bn so far, Hegseth says, as Pentagon seeks billions more
byline: The war with Iran has cost the US some $37.5bn (£28bn) so far - an increase of nearly $8bn since the last estimate in May, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

title: Zelensky sacks Ukraine’s top army commander after days of protests
byline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has dismissed the country’s army commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

title: Police urge vehicle rental firms to tighten security amid rising fraud
byline: Police have urged vehicle rental companies to strengthen their security measures, warning that fraudsters are using fake identities, suspicious payment methods and deceptive tactics to obtain rental vehicles before disappearing without a trace.

title: June inflation jumps to 6.5%
byline: Headline inflation accelerated to 6.5 percent in June from 5.4 percent in May, driven by rising transport and food prices, as consumer prices continued to edge higher despite the economy’s broader recovery.

title: State entities face heat over delayed annual reports and financial mismanagement
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya this week rebuked ministries and state institutions over years-long delays in filing annual reports and financial statements, revealing that some audit reports remain pending after several years.

title: Former State Minister’s son arrested over Rs. 20M robbery
byline: The son of former State Minister Shanta Bandara has been arrested by the Colpetty Police in connection with the alleged robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

title: CIABOC begins probe on former Minister Akila Viraj
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) has launched an investigation into allegations that former United National Party (UNP) General Secretary Akila Viraj Kariyawasam committed an offence of corruption by recruiting employees to the Presidential Secretariat and deploying them for his personal and political activities.

title: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra detained by Delhi Police amid protest near PM residence
byline: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by the Delhi Police on Tuesday while leading a protest near Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s official residence at Lok Kalyan Marg, where Congress leaders were demanding accountability over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and seeking the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

title: Pakistan steps in as US-Iran war widens and Hormuz shipping stalls
byline: Diplomatic efforts intensified on Tuesday to revive the collapsed interim agreement between Iran and the United States, even as both sides continued attacks for a 10th day of renewed fighting. Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni travelled to Pakistan, which has been trying to mediate between the two countries, but it was not immediately clear what fresh arrangement could emerge to end the war.

title: Crossings dominate market activity as ASPI extends decline
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange ended Tuesday’s session on a mixed note, with the ASPI closing lower despite a strong start to the day, as renewed selling pressure erased early gains. The benchmark index climbed nearly 70 points within the first 15 minutes of trading, supported by buying interest in selected large-cap counters. However,

title: Govt. has purchased over 1,900 metric tons of paddy since July
byline: The government has purchased a total of 1,910 metric tons of paddy as of yesterday (20), Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: My last days in Parliament: MP Archchuna
byline: Referring to his political future, independent MP Ramanathan Archchuna today said he is currently spending his last days in Parliament.

title: Dengue risk to remain high for next three weeks: Health Minister
byline: The risk of dengue transmission in Sri Lanka is expected to remain elevated for the next three weeks, with the period leading up to mid-August identified as a high-risk phase, Cabinet Spokesperson and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: Full probe ordered into Homagama factory fire that killed five
byline: Labour Deputy Minister Mahinda Jayasinghe has instructed officials of the Labour Department to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the fire that broke out at a factory in the Katuwana Industrial Zone, Homagama, this morning (21), and submit a report urgently.

title: Special Cabinet panel reviews preparedness for possible El Niño impacts
byline: The Special Cabinet Subcommittee and Officials’ Committee appointed to assess measures in response to possible El Niño conditions met for the second time at the Presidential Secretariat yesterday (20).

title: PM meets UK delegation on rabies eradication
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya today (21) held discussions with a delegation from the United Kingdom on implementing a more systematic and accelerated national programme to eradicate rabies, improve animal welfare and manage Sri Lanka’s stray dog population.

title: Trump wants to nominate FIFA chief for UN secretary-general: Report
byline: US President Donald Trump wants FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be the next secretary-general of the UN, the New York Post reported Tuesday.

title: Rubio says US still willing to negotiate over Iran crisis
byline: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said ​on Wednesday the United States is still willing to negotiate an end to the Iran crisis but Tehran is not serious about talks, as the widening conflict disrupted two of ‌the world’s most critical energy chokepoints.

title: Kusal Mendis ruled out of remaining LPL 2026 matches
byline: Colombo Kaps captain Kusal Mendis has been ruled out of the remainder of the Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026 after sustaining a hamstring injury.

title: Ex-Australia batter David Warner pleads guilty to drink driving
byline: Former Australia batter David Warner has pleaded guilty to drink driving, after being charged following a random breath test in Sydney in April.

title: Public invited to name Pinnawala Zoo’s three fishing cat cubs
byline: As Sri Lanka prepares to celebrate World Cat Day on August 8, Pinnawala Zoo has opened a public naming competition for its three adorable Fishing Cat cubs, inviting animal lovers to suggest creative and meaningful names for the young felines.

title: Ven. Omalpe Sobhitha Thera resigns as Chief Sangha Nayaka
byline: Ven. Dr. Omalpe Sobhitha Thera has resigned from the post of Chief Sangha Nayaka of the Southern Province of the Sri Lanka Ramanna Maha Nikaya after serving in the position for 14 years.

title: Some Presidential palaces converted into court houses: PM
byline: Some Presidential palaces have been converted into court houses, while others will be used for economically viable purposes, Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament today.

title: Veterinarians urge swift passage of Animal Welfare Act
byline: The Association of Veterinarians for Humane Management of Animal Population has urged authorities not to further delay the enactment of the Animal Welfare Act, warning that continued delays would prolong the suffering of animals.

title: Dengue cases climb to 78,125
byline: The number of dengue cases reported in Sri Lanka so far this year has increased to 78,125, according to the latest data released by the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU).

title: Southern Province Grade 9 Civic Education exam postponed over question paper delay
byline: The Grade 9 Civic Education examination paper scheduled to be held today has been postponed in the Southern Province due to the failure to receive the printed question papers at zonal education offices.

title: Ownership of Water supply and drainage projects under NWSDB to be changed?
byline: Ownership of water supply and drainage projects coming under the purview of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) and local bodies are to be changed under the proposed National Water Supply and Drainage Board Amendment Bill which was tabled in Parliament yesterday.

title: Stop harassing businessmen: Opposition MP
byline: The Government has to stop harassing local businessmen, Opposition MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake said focusing on the arrest of House of Fashion owner whom he revealed has been sent behind bars for undervaluing his assets.

title: France becomes first EU country to ban social media access for under-15s
byline: France’s parliament has approved a bill banning social media access for children under 15, making it the first EU country to bar children from apps such as TikTok.

title: Tunnel collapse in India kills 12 workers
byline: At least 12 workers were killed after a portion of an under-construction tunnel collapsed following a gas explosion in India’s north-eastern Sikkim state, officials said.

title: Tokyo urges men to wear shorts to work, but some women say it’s ’leg hair harassment’
byline: As temperatures rise this summer, Japanese men are baring more leg at work than ever before.

title: Defence Adviser to Indian HC calls on Navy Commander
byline: The Defence Adviser to the High Commission of India in Colombo, Captain M Anand called on Commander of the Navy, Vice Admiral Damian Fernando at the Navy Headquarters today, 22 July 2026.

title: PM reviews progress of education digitalisation programme
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has reviewed the progress of Sri Lanka’s education digitalisation programme and future initiatives aimed at strengthening digital facilities in schools.

title: Pakistan seeks $10 billion fund from US after mediating Iran talks, source says
byline: Pakistan has asked the United States for a $10 billion exchange stabilization facility, according to a source briefed on the matter, which, if approved, could provide a lifeline for the cash-strapped South ​Asian economy.

title: Rs. 50mn worth illegal smartphones seized at Liberty Plaza
byline: More than 300 illegally imported high-end smartphones, including the latest Apple iPhone models, with an estimated value of around Rs. 50 million have been seized during a raid at a shop in Colombo’s Liberty Plaza.

title: India opposition leader Gandhi freed after detention at student-led protest
byline: Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has been released after he was detained during growing protests over the education system.

title: Ministry of Transport, Highways gets new Secretary
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed Eng. (Dr.) Asiri Karunawardena as the new Secretary to the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development, the President’s Media Division said.

title: DNA tests underway to confirm identities of victims in Homagama factory fire
byline: Authorities have commenced DNA testing to officially confirm the identities of five employees who died in a major fire at a helmet manufacturing factory in the Katuwana Industrial Estate, Homagama.

title: Largest marine plastic waste stock sent for recycling after MSC ELSA 3 spill
byline: The largest quantity of marine plastic waste collected following the MSC ELSA 3 maritime incident has been officially cleared for recycling, marking a major milestone in Sri Lanka’s coastal clean-up efforts, Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody said.

title: Date fixed for no-confidence motion debate against Justice Minister
byline: Parliament will debate the no-confidence motion against Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara on Friday, the Parliament Media Unit said.

title: Wildlife holiday bungalows to be upgraded
byline: The government has planned to upgrade holiday bungalows managed by the Departments of Wildlife Conservation and Forest Conservation, using modern technology to provide improved facilities for the public.

title: Toxic alcohol addiction changes brain chemistry: Psychotherapist
byline: Addiction to toxic alcohol can disrupt the brain’s natural reward system by triggering excessive releases of dopamine, leading to long-term changes in brain function, Counselor and Psychotherapist Dr. Chaminda Weerasiriwardane said.

title: Sri Lanka passport rises to 94th in 2026 Henley Index
byline: Sri Lanka’s passport has improved its position to 94th place in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, recording its highest ranking in recent years.

title: Strong wind advisory issued for several areas
byline: The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre has issued a strong wind advisory for the Northern and North-central provinces, as well as Hambantota and Trincomalee districts, effective until 11.00 a.m. tomorrow (23).

title: DAPH calls for coordinated plan to eliminate rabies by 2030
byline: The Department of Animal Production and Health (DAPH) has called for a planned and humane approach to eliminate rabies in Sri Lanka by 2030, highlighting the need for cooperation among government institutions, veterinarians, local authorities and animal welfare organisations.

title: Criminal record or false info could permanently block US entry: Embassy
byline: The U.S. Embassy in Colombo has warned visa applicants that criminal convictions and false information provided during the application process could lead to permanent restrictions on entering the United States.

title: Singer “Chili” fined for attempted assault on police officers
byline: Singer Thilanka Vidusha alias “Chili”, who obstructed the duty of the police officers, intimidated and attempted to assault them was found guilty by Kaduwela Magistrate Aruna Indrajith today and fined Rs. 6000.

title: Sri Lanka’s exports surpass US$9 billion in first half of 2026
byline: Sri Lanka’s total exports exceeded the US$9 billion mark during the first six months of 2026, reflecting continued growth in both merchandise and services exports despite challenges in several key sectors.

title: China ready to work with Sri Lanka to build strategic trust: Chinese Ambassador
byline: Military cooperation between China and Sri Lanka has been further deepened in multiple fields in recent years, covering defense consultations, personnel training, equipment and technical exchanges, Chinese Ambassador to Sri Lanka Qi Zhenhong said.
